biography.plain_text: Santiago Eduardo Soulas was an Argentine industrialist and landowner from a French family established in the wool trade. He presided over Eduardo Soulas Ltda., the family firm's financial and industrial successor, whose interests included textiles, leather, footwear and banking. His Argentine property included the San Vicente ranch near Mar del Plata.

long_biography.plain_text:
At the Chateau de Baillon in France, Santiago Soulas commissioned formal gardens from Achille Duchene and added stables and greenhouses. The Argentine industrialist's alterations became part of the village's history: the adjacent street was named in his honour. He also commissioned a country house at San Vicente, where the estate raised sheep and pedigree livestock.

His collecting extended from French furniture to illustrated books. He owned eighteenth-century cabinetmaking, a suite of Jacob chairs and a painting by Maurice Utrillo. At the dispersal of Matias Errazuriz's library, he acquired a volume of David's Psalms with royal provenance and an album containing drawings by Empress Eugenie.
